title: Panel Matching — explainable scores, a different ranking for every paper
story: Miguel Yu's Form 1 and concept papers have been verified and endorsed ({case:research_title}). Panel Matching now reads the body text of the three concept papers and compares it with what the Graduate School has recorded about each faculty member: research interests, publications, past advisee and panel titles, degrees and the profile specialization. The research title and the file names are shown for reference but are left out of the comparison.

The point for the panel: the recommendation is explained, not a black box. Every candidate gets a score out of 100 made of three visible parts (expertise 60 points, availability 25, workload 15), the screen names the method used, shows the topics in common, and the student's adviser is excluded from the panel. To show that the ranking follows the paper, the same screen is then opened for the seven demo papers GS-2026-PM-01 to PM-07, which belong to different fields, and each one produces a different top of the list.
accounts: Opens Panel Matching, reviews the ranking, selects the panel and finalizes it; opens the Faculty page
data: Miguel Yu, 2260004, MAED (key research-miguel); Title Defense package from the previous case
GS-2026-PM-01 Camille Dizon (MSN), PM-02 Rafael Ocampo (MAPSY), PM-03 Jasper Lorenzo (MSCS), PM-04 Bea Fontanilla (MBA), PM-05 Miko Almario (MBA), PM-06 Liza Marquez (DBA), PM-07 Nico Baltazar (MBA)
Content Specialist: the suggested Dr. Celeste Tan replaced by Dr. Patricia Salvador (rank 3)
For Dr. Teresa Lim, kind Research interest: "Trust, perceived risk, and adoption of digital wallets among young working adults" (added to show the score react, then removed again)

parts.title: Part A — Miguel Yu: how the ranking is built
parts.intro: Sign in as GS Staff. The wide candidate table is wider than its card on a normal screen; the screenshots in this part were taken with the window widened so that all four columns show at once.

steps.text: Open **5 · Panel Matching**, search for **2260004** and select **Miguel Yu**. Confirm that the page heading is Panel Matching and that the selected student reads 2260004 - Yu, Miguel - MAED. Note the **Rules applied on this screen** bar (11 rules from the Graduate School policies, 2 need review).

shots.caption: Panel Matching with Miguel Yu selected, and the rules bar for this screen.

steps.text: Read the green box under **Panel recommendation workspace**: "Three concept papers content ready", 3 of 3 PDFs uploaded and 3 of 3 successfully read, with the note that research titles and file names are excluded. Confirm the method badge **Similarity match (keyword TF-IDF)** and the line "Paper analysis: Keyword analysis (local, no AI service)".

shots.caption: Source and method: three papers read, keyword TF-IDF similarity, no AI service.

steps: Read the keywords extracted from the papers (for example machine learning, learning analytics, student engagement, learning management system) and the three paper cards. Each card lists the file name, the badge Text extracted, the analyzed keywords and an excerpt, so staff can see exactly what the system read. The research title is printed on the screen as display only.

steps.text: Scroll to the three coloured boxes: **60 pts** Expertise match (paper vs. faculty records), **25 pts** Availability (conflict-free windows), **15 pts** Workload (other student panels). Then read the sentence that the thesis panel needs 3 members (Panel Chair, Content Specialist, Method Specialist) and the red note **Not eligible for this student's panel**: Dr. Liwayway Bautista, adviser of this student, cannot sit on the student's panel.

shots.caption: The three scoring parts, the panel size and the adviser exclusion.

steps.text: Scroll to the ranked table **Ranked panel candidates**. The screen shows the top 11 candidates. Read the first rows: rank 1 **Dr. Marlon Geronimo 90.3/100** (expertise 60/60, availability 20.3/25, workload 10/15; 4 conflict-free windows, 2 other student panels), rank 2 **Dr. Celeste Tan 70.4/100** (41.3/60, 14.1/25, 15/15; Limited availability), rank 3 **Dr. Patricia Salvador 66.9/100** (39.7/60, 17.2/25, 10/15), rank 4 Dr. Daniel Uy 51.5/100, rank 5 **Dr. Teodoro Ramos 51/100** (36.9/60, 14.1/25, 0/15) with the amber flag Overloaded (7 other student panels). The topic chips in each row (for example educational data, machine learning, data mining for Dr. Geronimo) are the terms the paper and the faculty records share. The green rows are the suggested panel: Chair Geronimo, Content Specialist Tan, Method Specialist Ramos.

shots.caption: Ranked candidates for Miguel Yu with the score bar and the three parts of each score.

steps.text: Click **Why this score** on rank 1. Read **How the score was built** (Expertise 60 / 60, Availability 20.3 / 25, Workload 10 / 15, Total 90.3 / 100), the sentence on how expertise is scaled across the candidate pool, and the line "Method: Similarity match (keyword TF-IDF) (similarity 0.3049)". Read **Passage of the paper that matched** and **Expertise records used**: a Publication (2023), the profile Specialization and a Research interest, each with the words that matched and the tag Demo data. Click **Hide why** again.

shots.caption: Why Dr. Geronimo scores 90.3: components, similarity value, matching passage and the expertise records used.

parts.title: Part B — Select the panel, appoint the chair, finalize

steps.text: Scroll to **Review and adjust the panel set**. The suggested panel is preselected in the three seat lists: **Panel Chair** #1 Dr. Marlon Geronimo - 90.3/100, **Content Specialist** #2 Dr. Celeste Tan - 70.4/100, **Method Specialist** #5 Dr. Teodoro Ramos - 51/100. Under **Panel composition rules** every check shows a tick: all 3 seats filled, every role seated once, different faculty in every seat, adviser not on the panel, Dr. Geronimo chairs the panel (University-affiliated faculty), no External Panel seat for a thesis, and Dr. Ramos has recorded research-methods expertise.

shots.caption: The seat lists with the suggested panel and the composition rules from the Research Protocol.

steps.text: To show that staff decide, open the **Content Specialist** list and choose **#3 Dr. Patricia Salvador - 66.9/100** instead of Dr. Tan. Keep Dr. Geronimo as **Panel Chair** (this is how the chair is appointed: the seat named Panel Chair).

shots.caption: Content Specialist changed to Dr. Salvador; chair and method seats unchanged.

steps.text: Click **Finalize selected panel**. Confirm that the status badge above the seats changes to **Final panel selected** and that the button now reads **Update final panel**.

shots.caption: Final panel selected: Geronimo (Chair), Salvador (Content), Ramos (Method).

steps.text: Open **4 · Research Gate**, search for Miguel Yu and scroll to the **Panel Matching** card. It now shows the badge **Final panel selected** with the three names (Dr. Marlon Geronimo, Dr. Patricia Salvador, Dr. Teodoro Ramos) instead of "Recommended panel available". The panelists then receive an invitation in the Faculty Portal (Panel Invitations) and the chair's seat is the one that later records the verdict; Defense Scheduling is the next case ({case:defense-scheduling}).

shots.caption: Research Gate showing that the panel is in place.

notes: Score = expertise similarity (60) + availability (25) + workload (15). Availability counts conflict-free defense windows (8 windows earn full marks). Workload counts other student panels; four or more other panels carries the Overloaded flag.

The method label on every screen in this run is Similarity match (keyword TF-IDF), computed locally with no AI service. When an embeddings key is configured the same screen shows Semantic match (Gemini embeddings) instead; that was not enabled in this run and is not shown here.
The faculty expertise records are demonstration data written for the capstone (tag Demo data), not real USLS faculty records. The stakeholder's real records are still to be provided.

Candidates who share no topic with the paper are listed after those who do, even if their availability or workload points are higher; that is why a lower-scoring faculty member can rank above a higher-scoring one.

The suggested seats are a recommendation only; staff may change any seat. The protocol checks (adviser not on the panel, all seats filled, chair from the University faculty) are repeated on the server when the panel is finalized. The research-methods expertise check for the Method Specialist is advisory.
The panelists answer a panel invitation in their own Faculty Portal; a declined seat creates a task for the Research Coordinator to replace the panelist.
